narration: Welcome to the Central Asian Antiquities gallery. This is a fragment of a Buddhist wall painting from Miran in Xinjiang, dating to the 3rd–4th century CE. The piece is painted pigment on stucco and measures about 40 by 55 centimeters, showing part of a donor’s face and shoulder in a style that blends Gandharan and Central Asian conventions. It was recovered by Sir Aurel Stein during his early 20th‑century expeditions along the Silk Route, and now forms part of our collection of around 600 objects from those journeys. The painting offers a glimpse into the multicultural Buddhist world that flourished in the oasis towns of Central Asia.
